name: Fertiliser supply
summary: Egyptian urea near $535 a tonne after gas cuts; Gulf nitrogen exports still depend on an impeded Strait of Hormuz
state: Egyptian granular urea fetched about $535 a tonne in November contracts after gas supplies to fertiliser plants were rationed from 1 Nov (Fertilizer Daily, 9 Nov; UkrAgroConsult). Gulf exports rely on the Strait of Hormuz, where Iran's Revolutionary Guards said on 26 Nov they are keeping the strait closed after two tankers hit mines (Baird Maritime, Reuters). No export bans by several major exporters were found as of 26 Nov, so Watch holds.
for_you: Farmers face high nitrogen costs for spring planting, which can feed through to food prices next year.
rubric_hit: Major exporter's gas-driven supply curbs and an impeded export route = Watch; no multi-exporter bans

sources.title: Fertilizer Daily — Egyptian urea price rises on gas cuts
UkrAgroConsult — Egyptian urea prices rise to $535 per ton amid gas supply restrictions
Baird Maritime — Iran says two tankers exploded after hitting sea mines near Oman

why: Fertiliser prices lead food prices by months; much of the world's urea and ammonia is exported from Russia, the Gulf and China.
drivers: Gas prices, Gulf shipping, export bans and quotas, sanctions, planting seasons.

rubric.alert: Urea up more than 60% in three months, several major exporters restricting at once, or a key export route closed.
rubric.watch: Urea up more than 30% in three months, or a major exporter restricts exports.
rubric.normal: Urea and ammonia prices within their normal range; no major export restrictions.
